decisions.reason: As an extension of the established offer with its own product page, it likely meets at least modest aspirations and a medium-sized R&D-active firm in a growing market has enough slack to continue it.

The digital twin service fits the firm's geospatial integration direction, and despite weaker website prominence the strategic relevance and uncertainty typical of new services make continued experimentation more likely than withdrawal.

Because it is close to the core offer but only lightly signaled and overlaps functionally with other identity products, it faces the most internal comparison pressure, yet the firm would still likely keep it while learning about demand.

An open GIS development framework supports the firm's platform-oriented capabilities and complements consulting and engineering work, so behavioral decision-making would favor retention unless clear underperformance appears.

The explicitly announced identity service is closely tied to GIS integration needs and appears strategically sponsored, so with no strong evidence of failure the firm would likely keep it on the market.
